This was my first "found phone" type of mystery/horror to play so I was quite intrigued by the concept and mechanics as a whole. It really challenged how well of a snoop you were sometimes. Hilariously, I kept getting all the bad choices that ultimately led me to getting probably the worst ending possible and I wasn't really upset by that. However, there were some aspects that were a bit troubling for me throughout my playthrough. 

The jumpscares were considerably louder than the rest of the game and there are no audio options available. I guess I could understand if that was intentional since the "investigation" periods are very quiet (aside from [spoiler]the random knocks which were genuinely terrifying because I thought they were happening IRL[/spoiler]), but I actually did have fun just snooping through/messing with Anna's phone and texting everyone, so the cheap jumpscares took me out of the game pretty often.

Also, the climax (and the ending as a whole) just didn't totally sit right with me for some reason. Maybe my focus was waning by that point, but with hardly enough exposition to help drive the antagonist's motives, it just felt very out of left field. (Okay, maybe if I hadn't gone into this game ≈99% blind and maybe had also known [spoiler]what a simulacrum was[/spoiler], I would've had a better idea of what I was getting myself into.) With all that being said, I was left feeling underwhelmed and unsatisfied.

At the end of the day, SIMULACRA was [b]just okay[/b]. It's already very cheap in price, but I recommend you buy it during a sale if you're really that interested. I have just a small shred of hope for improvement on the second game.

The ending does come a bit abruptly with a long, Twilight Zone-esque info dump and I wasn't entirely satisfied, but it's a 'light' horror game, so I wasn't expecting sunshine and rainbows.

Simulacra wasn't an entirely bad experience. I actually had a decent time with most of the game. However, the overall package is important to me with a game. I only played through Mass Effect 3 once because the endings were so off-putting that I did not have any interest in playing through again because the conclusion lowered the quality of the game as a whole for me. Mind you, Simulacra doesn't have two games that came before it to ruin the legacy of or anything, nor is it even a tenth the length of Mass Effect 3, but an unsatisfying conclusion to any heavily story-focused game is often the ruin of many a game that were doing well up until that point.

With Simulacra, you navigate a missing girl's cell phone, using the text messaging, web browser, social media posts, and a dating app to further your investigation into where the girl is, gain a couple of allies to help with said investigation, and ultimately conclude with a villain which I won't spoil the identity of or anything like that. I will say that you should be able to easily understand a great villain when the villain monologues to you about why said villain is doing things, and there should be some logical explanations for the reasoning for the villain's actions, etc. Also, a villain shouldn't just pop out of nowhere, typically. Imagine if you got to the end of a deep storyline, and suddenly an extraterrestrial pops out without proper foreshadowing. It would make for a "good bad movie," but a terrible plot point. Again, I won't say specifics about this villain, but the villain does not seem to have a very logical viewpoint, and the villain pops practically out of nowhere and can do things that the game never explains which are vital to the main storyline.

Finally, there appear to be four different endings. Apparently the game locks you out of certain endings based on certain actions you take at some point in the game. I have no idea what those actions were or when they came up. Worse yet, there is no manual saving in Simulacra. There is ONE autosave file that overwrites every time you complete an objective, meaning to see the other endings, you have to start the game from the beginning again. The text messages pop up faster than before, but the game still takes too long for me to have the patience to play through it again, especially since the gameplay wasn't particularly enjoyable for me. Simulating a real cell phone was a cool premise, but it wasn't "fun" to interact with for me outside of the initial surprises of what the very small cast of characters (and an even smaller cast of *relevant* characters) have to say.

The ending I got was horribly dark and unpleasant, and the other ending that was offered to me was clearly going to be horribly dark and unpleasant as well. Dark endings can be entertaining if the storyline gives a satisfying quality to them that doesn't leave you feeling cheated. In Simulacra, the villain effectively tells you "lulz, you made decisions (that I'm not going to specify which ones or when) which set this stuff up. Now make horrible choice A, or horrible choice B." I stopped caring about the story immediately upon being given these options, and just proceeded to the ending knowing my conclusion was going to suck because I didn't play with a walkthrough and the game doesn't allow saving aside from the regularly-overwriting autosave, so you can't just load back a few minutes to make a different decision and see things play out differently.

Without very clear points of making relevant decisions, and without a manual save you can load, AND without enjoyable dark/"bad" endings, Simulacra left me disappointed in what initially seemed like a game I was going to talk about to others and say great things about it, but walling off endings sneakily and overwriting autosaves without a manual save option ruined the overall package of this game for me. I already regret the time I spent on it and I'm not going to waste any more of my time looking up the other endings online or replaying it. I will forever remember the crap ending choice the game locked me into and look back on Simulacra with disdain and disappointment.

I already own the sequel, Simulacra 2, but I no longer intend to play it because I dislike the first game so much now.

I got this game today and I was incredibly excited to play. I did around 4 playthroughs, trying to see the easter eggs and gather all the achievements and overall I'm rather amazed.

The use of real people in a game was a new concept to me but I enjoyed the idea a lot, especially since it highlighted the possible dangers of the digital world and made them more transferrable to the real world. The voice acting was a bit unrealistic sometimes but that's a minor issue. 

There are 5 possible endings (though the game at the end shows you only four of them) and your choices really impact them. The dialogue options that the game revolves around either make or break your case, so you have to think about what to choose.

The game is rather easy, in most cases if you get stuck at anything either of the two characters that you keep talking to will help you. 

After over 6 hours of playthrough, I have to say I am really impressed with this game. It was my first time ever playing something of this format and I will now have expectations for the future. I would not count this game as a horror, since the repeated jumpscares and glitches were far from scary (but maybe they might scare some people, who knows!). The true scary theme in the game is the realization that people on the Internet might really be bad and you shouldn't trust everyone you meet online. 

Even though it's common knowledge, when showcased like this, it can be eye-opening to some. Great game.

Simulacra is a special and different game, i could say it a simulator/visual novel through a phone. In the begging, you found a mobile phone, that a girl lost but she also went missing. As you keep trying to find the girl, the story is going weirder and weirder( in a good way).It have a lot of texting and reading, so you can fill the gaps. The good thing is that all the reading is more like a chat so it flows smoothly. The game have a lot of endings, and after you beat it for the 1st time it unlocks the Begin+ mode, so you can go faster through the same texts. I try to get every ending and it took me around 6 hours. The background sound was a nice touch. Something that i found as con was that there is only 1 save and not multiple, so you can load and get faster some endings. Overall, i was suprised from this game in a very good way and i am gonna play the second game for sure

Το Simulacra είναι ένα ιδιαίτερο και διαφορετικό παιχνίδι, θα το χαρακτήριζα ως simulator/ visual novel μέσα από κινητό. Ξεκινάς έχοντας στη κατοχή σου ένα χαμένο κινητό, το οποίο ανήκει σε μια κοπέλα η οποία έχει μυστηριωδώς εξαφανιστεί. Προσπαθείς να εντοπίσεις αυτό το άτομο για να του επιστρέψεις το κινητό αλλά στη πορεία εξελίσσεται σε μια ιδιαίτερα και περίεργη ιστορία. Έχει αρκετό chatting και ψάξιμο πληροφοριών για να συνδέσεις κενά. Το καλό είναι ότi ενώ έχει διάβασμα, είναι σε μορφή συνομιλίας οπότε φεύγει πιο εύκολα. Έχει αρκετά διαφορετικά τέλη. Μετά το πρώτο play-through υπάρχει η επιλογή Begin+ στην οποία το chat είναι πολύ πιο γρήγορο. Προσωπικά δοκίμασα όλα τα διαφορετικά τέλη και μου πήρε συνολικά γύρω στις 5-6 ώρες. Οι διάφοροι ήχοι που παίζουν στο πίσω μέρος του παιχνιδιού είναι ωραία πινελιά. Κάτι που βρήκα σαν αρνητικό είναι ότι, υπάρχει ένα save και όχι αρκετά ώστε να μπορείς να κάνεις load σε κάποια στιγμή, για να αποφύγεις κάποια “περιττά” κομμάτια όταν κυνηγάς διαφορετικό τελείωμα. Ευχάριστη έκπληξη και σίγουρα θα δοκιμάσω και το δεύτερο παιχνίδι.
